site.title: Fullstack Engineer
site.oneLiner: Fullstack engineer for fintech and B2B SaaS: data-heavy dashboards, real-time interfaces, payment flows and the APIs behind them.
bio: I work on the parts of a product that have to hold up under real conditions: fintech dashboards with live balances, crypto banking flows across 24+ currencies, BI tools filtering and exporting 100,000+ orders without stalling the tab.

The toolkit shifts from project to project; the actual job is judgment: knowing when a virtualized table beats pagination, when a live connection beats polling, when a shared component library saves the next six months of work.
Sometimes that means building on top of a design system someone else shipped; other times there's no designer on the team at all, and every interface decision is mine to make, start to finish.

grx.summary: Owned the GRX Pay frontend and the shared component library behind the products of a Swiss fintech: crypto-fiat payments, tokenized real-world assets and a retail exchange.

ezcloud.summary: Led fullstack work for a US-based B2B SaaS and e-commerce intelligence company: Amazon seller analytics, product sourcing, a phone top-up platform, ad-campaign tooling, online art auctions and a lab system for a biobank, all on a shared design system. Owned interface design with no dedicated designer.

grx-pay.name: GRX Pay
grx-pay.description: A crypto payment gateway: merchant dashboard, admin panel and hosted payment pages, with real-time balances across 24+ currencies.
grx-pay.overview: GRX Pay lets businesses accept crypto. Merchants issue invoices and payment links, take funds in any supported coin and network, convert, and withdraw in crypto or euros via SEPA. The platform team verifies merchants and controls fees, limits and every operation from an admin panel.
grx-pay.challenge: Three audiences, three apps, one product: merchants managing money, a compliance and finance team watching it, and buyers who pay once and never come back. Payments pass through many states, from network confirmations to underpayment and compliance blocks, and each one has to be clear to the person on the other side.
approach: Micro-frontends with a BFF layer that shapes data from the backend microservices per page, with performance budgeted from day one.

Hosted payment pages cover the full lifecycle: currency and network choice with the fee shown up front, QR and timer, network confirmations, paid late, underpaid with a top-up, expired, blocked by compliance.
Withdrawals run as a wizard with saved recipients and status tracking. Mass payouts upload a CSV, validate every row, catch duplicates, and preview fees and balance before launch.
Compliance built into the UI: KYC/KYB through Sumsub, Chainalysis risk scores and blocks on invoices, Travel Rule details.
Admin: a merchant card with 10 tabs. Fee and limit groups are edited inline in the grid, and a conflict dialog resolves edits when two people change the same group.
outcome: currencies and networks, balances live over WebSocket
Lighthouse score, mobile LCP under 1.5s

grx-public-platform.name: GRG Public Platform
grx-public-platform.description: The public face of a Swiss fintech: marketing site, waitlists, careers and API docs, on one shared design system.
grx-public-platform.overview: GRG builds payments (GRX Pay), a retail exchange and real-world asset tokenization. The public platform brings in merchants and leads, collects waitlists for products still in development, hires through Careers, and documents the API for integrators.
grx-public-platform.challenge: One brand across two apps, the site and the docs, several products at different stages, and a fintech security bar. Analytics and reCAPTCHA still had to run under a strict content security policy.
approach: Turborepo monorepo: the site, the docs portal and {'@'}grx/ui share one design system (components, form wrappers, 300+ icons, a theme on CSS variables), with no duplicated code.
Strict CSP with a nonce per request, generated in middleware together with i18n routing. Analytics and reCAPTCHA load only after cookie consent.
Forms run through Server Actions: one Zod schema on client and server, reCAPTCHA v3, and leads delivered straight to Slack.
Careers pulls jobs from the HR system with a static fallback, so job pages stay indexed even when the HR API is down.
API reference rendered from the OpenAPI spec. The search index and per-page share images are built at build time, so search works without a backend.
outcome: components in {'@'}grx/ui, shared by 3 products
languages, detected automatically

enterprise-bi-dashboard.name: Ledgerline
enterprise-bi-dashboard.description: Profit analytics for Amazon sellers: true net margin per order, product and account, across 22 marketplaces.
enterprise-bi-dashboard.overview: Ledgerline turns raw Amazon sales, fees, ad spend and returns into a real P&L. Buyers, team managers and admins each see the part they own.
enterprise-bi-dashboard.challenge: Amazon reports revenue, not profit. Fees, ads and returns land days later, in different time zones and currencies. The numbers had to be right over 100,000+ orders, and the tables fast enough to work in every day.
approach: P&L math (fees, COGS, ads, returns, tax, ACoS, TACoS) lives in one pure domain package shared by server and client, so every screen computes margin the same way.
Built for scale from day one: virtualized tables and cursor pagination keep 100,000+ orders smooth to scroll, filter and export.
SP-API and Advertising API connected via OAuth across 22 marketplaces, with automatic token rotation and expiry alerts.
Imports map columns and log errors per row, then retry only the failed rows. Exports run in a background queue with live progress.
Alerts on price, Buy Box, rank, stock and returns, delivered over WebSocket, push and Slack.
Built on the shared EZCLOUD design system.
outcome: GMV across 30 seller accounts
orders, filtered and exported without a stall

sourcely.name: Sourcely
sourcely.description: Turns supplier price lists into buy decisions: matches each item to its Amazon listing and shows profit and ROI after fees.
sourcely.overview: Analysts upload a supplier price list. Sourcely matches it to Amazon listings, prices in every fee and moves each product through Review, Invest or Don't invest.
sourcely.challenge: Supplier files are large and messy, while Amazon and Keepa limit API calls. Decisions had to be fast, shared across the team and explainable: why a product was bought or skipped.
approach: Price lists parsed in a Web Worker with an instant preview and resumable enrichment that stays inside Amazon and Keepa rate limits.
UPC-to-ASIN matching with 90-day Keepa history. FBA/FBM, referral and seasonal storage fees computed down to net ROI.
A rules engine ("buy if…") previews how many products a rule will hit before saving. Manual overrides keep a reversible link to the rule.
Kanban pipeline with drag and drop and keyboard control, synced live for the whole team.
Migrated about 150 components from Vue 2 to Vue 3 and TypeScript over 3 months, with no feature freeze.
Built on the shared EZCLOUD design system.
outcome: products per catalog
analysts using it daily

dialtone.name: Dialtone
dialtone.description: Phone top-up and device rental platform for retail counters, with customer, owner and staff interfaces.
dialtone.overview: Dialtone runs a phone shop's counter: number top-ups, scheduled auto-refills and device rentals. It covers the staff screen, the owner's finances and a customer account.
dialtone.challenge: Real money moves at a busy counter on unreliable networks. A dropped connection or a double click must never charge a card twice, and a failed refill must never get lost.
approach: Card data is entered only in the payment provider's isolated fields. Idempotent payment requests stop double charges on retries or dropped connections.
PWA with offline mode: reference data cached locally, transactions queued and synced when the network returns.
Three-step refill wizard. Scheduled auto-refills with a failed-payment queue and one-click retry.
Six-step rental wizard with live device availability, deposits, tax, delivery, late fees and returns.
Withdrawals need a second person's approval. Receipts print straight to thermal printers, and barcode scanners identify SIMs.
Built on the shared EZCLOUD design system.
outcome: API operations, built end to end
role-based interfaces

ezcloud-design-system.name: EZCLOUD Design System
ezcloud-design-system.description: One design system from Figma tokens, built for React and Vue and used across EZCLOUD products, each with its own theme.
ezcloud-design-system.overview: EZCLOUD products run on two stacks. Instead of two diverging UIs, they share one design system: the same tokens and components in React and Vue, with a theme per product.
ezcloud-design-system.challenge: Data-heavy products need the same hard pieces again and again: tables, filters, money and number formatting, file imports, charts, wizards. Built separately per product and per stack, they drift apart and get fixed three times.
approach: Colors, type, radii and shadows come from Figma as tokens, so design and code use the same values and a theme is a set of tokens, not a fork.

20 ready blocks over the base components: app shell, data table with column presets, filter bar, date-range picker, file upload with column mapping, job progress, KPI card, 7 chart types, step wizard.
Loading, empty and error states are part of every component, not left to each screen.
A fix lands once and reaches every product: the step wizard was reworked in the shared component, and every app's wizards updated with it.
outcome: components and blocks (54 base, 20 composed)
Storybook stories, documented on 78 pages

heirwell.name: Heirwell
heirwell.description: Timed online auctions for a US art dealer: live bidding with a timer per lot, invoices paid online, and consignments from owners.
heirwell.overview: Heirwell runs timed online sales for a US art dealer. Every lot has its own clock, bids arrive in real time, and the winner pays an invoice online. Owners can also offer works for sale.
heirwell.challenge: The final seconds decide the sale. Bids flood in at once, a late bid extends the clock, and every visitor's clock is a little off. The result has to stay consistent under that load, while the site loads fast, ranks in search and looks like a premium auction house.
approach: Bids in the closing seconds go through a Redis lock and a Postgres transaction, so two bids can't both win. A late bid extends the lot, and when the timer ends the lot is re-read from the server.
Contract-first API: Orval turns the OpenAPI spec into types, TanStack Query hooks, Zod schemas and MSW mocks. The frontend runs ahead of the backend, and a contract change shows up as a type error.
Next.js Cache Components: server-rendered by default, with cached data and dynamic parts streamed through Suspense, so the first screen is fast and indexable.
Lot catalogue imports of tens of thousands of rows are streamed and processed in BullMQ workers, so a large upload never runs the API out of memory.
Stripe and PayPal webhooks pass through an idempotency table, so a duplicate webhook can't record a payment twice.
outcome: end-to-end specs on desktop Chrome and mobile Safari, each with accessibility checks
ways to pay (Stripe, PayPal, bank transfer), with webhooks that never record a payment twice

cryovault.name: Cryovault
cryovault.description: A lab system for a stem-cell biobank: batch tracking, electronic protocols with e-signatures, sample databases and a cryo-storage map, from intake to clinical release.
cryovault.overview: Cryovault follows every batch of stem cells through intake, processing, quality control, freezing and release. Lab staff fill electronic protocols, sign them, track samples in spreadsheet-like databases and see each vial's place in the cryo-storage.
cryovault.challenge: Clinical records leave no room for error. Formulas must compute themselves, a signed document must not change silently, and a vial's place in a dewar must match the database exactly while several people work at once.
approach: One form engine renders all 17 protocols from backend-defined JSON schemas: typed fields, dynamic sub-tables, calculated formula fields, draft autosave and validation that jumps to the broken field.
Signatures are confirmed with a password. A fully signed form locks, and unlocking it requires a reason that goes into the audit log.
Lab databases are editable grids with keyboard navigation, undo and CSV export, plus server-side edit locks so two people can't overwrite each other.
The cryo-storage map shows dewars, racks and boxes down to a single cell, with search by vial code and moves that check the cell is free.
Certificates and batch passports render as A4 print layouts, filled from the batch's forms, with missing sources highlighted.
outcome: clinical forms on one schema-driven form engine
user roles, each document signed and locked

wellbotany.name: Well Botany
wellbotany.description: A live online shop for herbs, supplements and organic food, which I build and run as the sole developer: storefront, checkout, customer accounts and an admin panel.
approach: Checkout runs in one database transaction. Conditional writes for stock and coupon limits mean the shop can't sell more than it has.
Postgres triggers record every price change. Each crossed-out price is counted from the lowest price of the last 30 days (EU Omnibus).
Stock syncs from the shop's Subiekt GT through xylem, a Windows service written in C#. It sends signed changes every 3 minutes and refuses broken snapshots.
The admin flags products missing data the law requires on a label: ingredients, warnings, serving size, photos.
CI runs every pull request on a fresh Neon branch. Nightly deploys migrate only on change, smoke-test and roll back on failure.
outcome: products, each with a full ingredient list
stock sync from the shop's ERP, through a Windows service in C#

seikatsu.name: seikatsu
seikatsu.description: My own app for money, tasks, books, habits, job search, car care and a wishlist. Installable, works offline, with an MCP server for AI assistants.
approach: Finance is double-entry: every transaction posts entries that sum to zero, in one database transaction, with exchange rates cached per day.
PSD2 bank sync and statement imports share one pipeline that skips records already imported.
Offline changes are queued and sent again when the connection returns, and each one is safe to send twice.
Server components read the database directly and changes go through server actions. No client cache; UI state lives in the URL.
Nightly encrypted backups are restored into a temporary Postgres to prove they work.
outcome: apps on one login, database and deploy
MCP tools that give AI assistants the same data

unitbot.name: unitbot
unitbot.description: A Claude Code agent that writes unit tests for each pull request, checks them with coverage and mutation testing, and opens them as a separate PR without touching production code.
approach: Changed files are classified without an LLM first. With nothing to test, the agent is not called at all.
Tests are checked with patch coverage and mutation testing, not only "they pass".
The agent's patch is verified again from scratch, with no secrets and with tooling from the base branch.
Hooks block writes outside test files and shell commands outside an allowlist.
A report is posted as one comment on the pull request. When existing tests fail, it reports a regression instead of rewriting them.
outcome: CI jobs, and only one of them holds the LLM key

aerolit.name: aerolit
aerolit.description: An operator dashboard for 240 air-quality sensors in Berlin, with key decisions written up as ADRs.
approach: The domain layer (AQI, trends, KPIs) is pure functions with no dependencies, enforced by ESLint and checked against figures computed separately in Python.
Cursor pagination in both directions. Search switches the table to a mode that covers the whole network and says so.
Light and dark themes from one token set, including map tiles and charts. Works from 2560px down to a phone, with nothing hover-only.
End-to-end tests at three widths, with axe checks in both themes.
outcome: sensors on a live map

hisashi.name: hisashi
hisashi.description: Turns the MacBook notch into a live panel for music, today's calendar, notifications, a file shelf, Claude Code sessions and CI runs.
approach: State lives in one pure reducer; the shell only feeds it events. That is also how these screenshots were made: the real views, rendered over demo state.
Claude Code hooks stream over a unix socket: the notch shows the current step and elapsed time, and single-choice questions can be answered from it.
GitHub Actions runs from every signed-in account. Failures stay with a rerun button.
The equalizer reads system audio levels through a Core Audio tap and an FFT. Nothing is recorded.
outcome: live feeds in one notch: music, calendar, notifications, Claude Code, CI

danylomorhun-com.name: danylomorhun.com
danylomorhun-com.description: This site: prerendered in 3 languages, with a WebGL hero, per-page share images and a blog.
approach: Every page and locale is prerendered and served from the CDN, each with its own canonical URL, hreflang, JSON-LD and sitemap entry.

The hero is a three.js scene with custom shaders. It starts once the page is idle, is skipped with reduced motion, Save-Data or low memory, runs at 30 fps at most and recovers from a lost WebGL context.
Each page gets its own share image per locale, rendered at build time.
The blog is a small Nuxt module: Markdown read at build time, code highlighted with Shiki, scheduled posts published by a daily workflow.
CI runs lint, type check, unit tests and Playwright with axe accessibility checks on every pull request.
outcome: LCP on Lighthouse's throttled mobile profile
Lighthouse accessibility, best practices and SEO
